## Nonstationary Gravity: Extension Track

A stationary field says how a settled source structures the stage. A changing source raises a further question: can that structure propagate causally while retaining the stationary map when the change stops? Chapter 3 has one action-supported scalar candidate and one more provisional directional PDE seed. They should not be merged into a single physical baseline.

### Scalar action-supported candidate

The scalar point-carrier action of the previous sections contains the field term

$$
S_\theta
=\frac{Z}{2}\int dt_*\,d^3x
\left(
\frac{\dot{\theta}^{2}}{c^2}
-\lvert\nabla\theta\rvert^2
\right),
$$

with carrier generator

$$
H_a=N(\theta)c
\sqrt{p_{f,a}^2+Q(\theta)p_a^2}.
$$

For the content-only branch, $\gamma=0$, and the normalized weak choice $\alpha=1$, variation gives

$$
\boxed{
\left(
\frac1{c^2}\partial_{t_*}^2-
\Delta
\right)
\theta
=\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^2}\rho_M},
\qquad
\rho_M:=\frac{\mathcal M}{c}.
$$

For compact prescribed source data, the retarded solution is

$$
\theta(t_*,\mathbf x)
=\frac{G_N}{c^2}
\int
\frac{
\rho_M(t_*-R/c,\mathbf x')
}{R}
\,d^3x',
\qquad
R:=\lvert\mathbf x-\mathbf x'\rvert.
$$

When the time derivatives vanish, this reduces exactly to

$$
\Delta\theta
=-\frac{4\pi G_N}{c^2}\rho_M,
$$

which is the achieved stationary scalar map.

The free scalar mode has positive energy because Newtonian normalization fixes

$$
Z=\frac{c^4}{4\pi G_N}>0.
$$

It propagates with $\omega^2=c^2k^2$, and the displayed carrier--field action supplies reciprocal local and integrated work. The same action also supplies the clock, ruler, massive/null map, and exact local $c$ described in Section 3.5.

These are substantial consistencies, but the status remains a point-carrier candidate. The source history must ultimately come from a conserved interacting matter model, not an arbitrary prescribed function. Bound matter, emission, screening, and the physical $\gamma=1$ readout are not jointly closed by this branch.

### Provisional vector PDE seed

The provisional transverse vector equation is

$$
\boxed{
\left(
\frac1{c^2}\partial_{t_*}^2-
\Delta
\right)
\mathcal A_i
=-\frac{16\pi G_N}{c^3}j_i^\perp,
\qquad
\partial_i\mathcal A_i=0}.
$$

As a PDE, it has the retarded Green solution

$$
\mathcal A_i(t_*,\mathbf x)
=-\frac{4G_N}{c^3}
\int
\frac{j_i^\perp(t_*-R/c,\mathbf x')}{R}
\,d^3x',
$$

and its stationary limit recovers the transverse Poisson equation. For the positive one-vector action normalization, $\mathcal A_i=-4\theta_i^\perp$.

Here $\mathcal A_i$ is the action/PDE coordinate, not the provisional observer-facing shift $A_i$. The field-side equation and its retarded solution do not establish a physical vector mode. The positive reciprocal one-vector action gives the wrong Lense--Thirring orientation, while an elliptic constrained response can fit the stationary sign only through an undetermined coefficient and supplies no causal observer transport. A closed current-work ledger, transported observer axes, a physical radiation observable, and the required rotating-source sign remain missing.

### Open completion layers

The two time-dependent equations therefore occupy different levels. The scalar candidate has a positive free mode, reciprocal point-carrier work, operational carrier variables, and exact stationary recovery. The vector equation has field-side mathematical consistency but not physical source-to-observer closure.

No nonlinear scalar/spatial equation, tensor source and action, radiative waveform sector, or exact rotating solution is adopted here. Those layers require their own sources, constraints, modes, work exchange, and observables before familiar coefficients or retarded forms can carry physical weight.

The nonstationary extension is thus real but narrow. It shows that the achieved scalar map can be embedded in a causal action-supported point-carrier candidate. It also preserves a precise vector PDE target. It does not yet provide a complete time-dependent theory of gravity.

The scalar action and work ledger are developed in [Appendix 3.7A](#sec-derivation-03-07A-scalar-nonstationary); the vector PDE and higher completion boundaries are collected in [Appendix 3.7B](#sec-derivation-03-07B-completion-boundaries).
